notes.1ai: Almost all candidates were able to recognise that the concentration in test-tube C would be half of that in test-tube B .
notes.1aii: Most candidates were awarded full marks for drawing the table. In some cases, candidates did not provide suitable headings or did not include units for the data collected. It is important that candidates do not include units in the body of the table.
notes.1aiii: This question required candidates to provide a suitable conclusion based on the data they collected. As they were measuring the time taken for the disc to rise in different concentrations of celery extract, they were required to provide a conclusion that showed a comparison between the high and low concentrations, rather than simply restating the data.
notes.1aiv: Some candidates find it difficult to identify the different variables in experiments. Many candidates were able to correctly identify the concentration of catalase as the independent variable but fewer were able to correctly identify the dependent variable as time.
notes.1bi: This question required candidates to explain how rate could be calculated. This proved to be challenging for many. Candidates needed to explain that to calculate rate, the distance travelled by the disc should be measured and then that value divided by the time taken to rise. The most common error was to divide the time by the distance or to not make it clear that the distance the disc travelled needed to be measured.
notes.1bii: Many candidates correctly identified errors in the method for both steps.
notes.1c: Some candidates had a very clear idea of how to plan a valid and reliable investigation that would measure the effect of sodium chloride concentration on the activity of catalase. Most candidates were able to discuss the need to control variables, such as the concentration of catalase and hydrogen peroxide or the temperature. Many were able to identify the need for repeats and a suitable safety precaution such as wearing gloves or goggles due to the hazards associated with the use of hydrogen peroxide solutions. A smaller number of candidates were able to correctly identify how the rate of reaction could be measured. A suitable method was to use a gas syringe to measure the volume of oxygen produced in a set time. It is important that candidates state a suitable range of values for the independent variable, rather than simply naming the independent variable.
notes.1d: The majority of candidates recalled that the presence of protein can be tested for using biuret reagent and that the positive test result would be purple.
notes.2ai: Candidates should be able to produce a biological drawing using a sharp pencil that exhibits clear and continuous lines. It is important that candidates do not use shading. High quality drawings showed the correct number of prickles on the leaf and the veins were carefully shown coming off the midrib.
notes.2aii: Many candidates were able to measure the length of line PQ within tolerance and also the length of the line on their drawing. The most common error was not using consistent units in the measurements. Without using the same unit to measure each line, the calculation would be incorrect. Another common error was giving the unit for magnification as millimetres.
notes.2bi: This question proved challenging for some candidates. Candidates were required to count the total number of leaves at 2.0 m above the ground, which was 50. They were then required to find the average number of prickles per leaf, which was 12. Some candidates instead calculated the average number of prickles from the table, rather than using the information provided in the stem of the question.
notes.2bii: Some candidates described ways to make the data more reliable rather than stating how the students had ensured the data was representative.
notes.2biii: The quality of the graph was very high for many candidates. Most were able to correctly label their axes, although a small number did not include units for the height above the ground. Most axes were suitably scaled and the plots were accurate. Drawing a suitable line of best fit is challenging for some candidates.
notes.2c: Most candidates were confident in recording the number of prickles and reading an appropriate value off their graph.
notes.2d: The majority of candidate correctly described the test for starch and the positive test result. Candidates would benefit from being specific in their answers. For instance, iodine solution rather than iodine and blue-black rather than black or dark blue.
